title: COPD stable management (GOLD ABE)
subject: respiratory
summary: Confirm COPD with post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC below 0.7, classify into GOLD group A, B or E, start a bronchodilator (A) or LABA+LAMA (B and E), add ICS only for exacerbations with blood eosinophils of 100 cells/microL or more (initially if 300 or more), and give smoking cessation, vaccination and pulmonary rehabilitation to all.

sections.title: Diagnose and assess
items: Spirometry is required: post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC below 0.7 in a patient with symptoms and exposure (tobacco, biomass smoke, occupational dust). Airflow grade: GOLD 1 FEV1 80% or more, GOLD 2 50 to 79%, GOLD 3 30 to 49%, GOLD 4 below 30% predicted.
Group A: 0 moderate or severe exacerbations in the past year and mMRC 0 to 1 or CAAT below 10. Group B: 0 exacerbations and mMRC 2 or more or CAAT 10 or more.
Group E (GOLD 2026): 1 or more moderate or severe exacerbations in the previous year, regardless of symptoms (a single moderate exacerbation now qualifies).

Measure the blood eosinophil count; it guides ICS use. Screen for comorbidities (cardiovascular disease, osteoporosis, anxiety, depression, lung cancer, OSA) and exclude asthma, bronchiectasis and TB sequelae.

sections.title: Initial pharmacological treatment
items: Group A: a bronchodilator for breathlessness, preferably long-acting (LAMA or LABA) if available and affordable; short-acting only for very occasional breathlessness.
Group B: LABA+LAMA combination. If a combination is unsuitable, either a LABA or a LAMA alone.
Group E: LABA+LAMA. Consider LABA+LAMA+ICS as initial therapy if blood eosinophils are 300 cells/microL or more.
LABA+ICS without a LAMA is not encouraged in COPD; if an ICS is indicated, use triple therapy. Patients with concomitant asthma must receive an ICS.
Prescribe a short-acting bronchodilator (salbutamol) for rescue in every group. Choose the device the patient can use and check technique at every visit.

sections.title: Follow-up: escalate or de-escalate
items: Review, assess technique and adherence, then adjust. Follow the exacerbation pathway if both dyspnoea and exacerbations are problems.
Dyspnoea on one long-acting bronchodilator: move to LABA+LAMA. Still breathless: switch device or molecule, add or intensify pulmonary rehabilitation, and look for other causes.
Exacerbations on monotherapy: LABA+LAMA. Exacerbations on LABA+LAMA: add ICS (triple) if eosinophils 100 cells/microL or more; benefit is greater with higher counts.
Exacerbations with eosinophils below 100, or despite triple therapy: azithromycin in non-smokers, or roflumilast if FEV1 below 50% with chronic bronchitis and a previous hospitalised exacerbation.
Despite triple therapy with eosinophils 300 cells/microL or more: consider dupilumab (with chronic bronchitis) or mepolizumab.

Withdraw ICS only if started inappropriately, ineffective, or causing significant side-effects or recurrent pneumonia; exacerbations are more likely after withdrawal if eosinophils are 300 or more. On LABA+ICS with further exacerbations: escalate to triple if eosinophils 100 or more, otherwise switch to LABA+LAMA.

sections.title: Non-pharmacological care and prevention
items: Smoking cessation at every visit: counselling plus nicotine replacement, varenicline or bupropion. Reduce biomass and occupational exposure.

Vaccination: annual influenza; pneumococcal (PCV20 or PCV21 preferred, or PCV15/PCV13 followed by PPSV23); RSV for eligible older adults or those with chronic lung disease; COVID-19 as per national advice; Tdap if not vaccinated in adolescence; shingles vaccine.
Pulmonary rehabilitation for all symptomatic patients: 6 to 8 week programme with supervised exercise at least twice weekly; start during or within 4 weeks after an exacerbation admission.
Written action plan, nutrition assessment, physical activity, and treatment of comorbidities according to their own guidelines.

sections.title: Oxygen, ventilation and advanced disease
items: Long-term oxygen therapy (at least 15 hours/day) if PaO2 55 mmHg (7.3 kPa) or less, or SaO2 88% or less, confirmed twice over 3 weeks; or PaO2 55 to 60 mmHg (SaO2 88%) with pulmonary hypertension, peripheral oedema or polycythaemia (haematocrit above 55%).
LTOT is not routinely indicated for moderate resting or exercise-induced desaturation.
Home NIV for persistent daytime hypercapnia, especially after a recent hospitalisation (PaCO2 above 53 mmHg 2 to 4 weeks after discharge); CPAP for coexisting obstructive sleep apnoea.
Refer selected patients with advanced emphysema for lung volume reduction or transplant assessment, and offer palliative care for refractory breathlessness.

sections.title: Monitoring
items: At each visit record symptoms (mMRC or CAAT), exacerbation frequency and severity, inhaler technique, adherence, side-effects and smoking status.
Spirometry at least annually and after significant change; recheck oxygenation for LTOT eligibility.
On azithromycin: baseline ECG for QTc and hearing check; exclude nontuberculous mycobacterial infection. On roflumilast: monitor weight, avoid if underweight, caution in depression.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Diagnosing COPD without spirometry, or missing asthma, bronchiectasis or post-TB lung disease.
Using ICS monotherapy or LABA+ICS as the default COPD inhaler.
Escalating drugs without checking technique and adherence, or without offering pulmonary rehabilitation.
Starting ICS in patients with eosinophils below 100 cells/microL, repeated pneumonia or previous mycobacterial infection.

drugs.name: Tiotropium (LAMA)
drugs.dose: 18 mcg by dry-powder inhaler once daily, or 5 mcg (2 puffs of 2.5 mcg) by soft mist inhaler once daily
drugs.notes: Caution in urinary retention and narrow-angle glaucoma.

drugs.name: Formoterol (LABA)
drugs.notes: Use as part of LABA+LAMA; not as monotherapy in anyone with asthma features.

drugs.name: Indacaterol-glycopyrronium (LABA+LAMA)
drugs.notes: Group B and E initial choice where available.

drugs.name: Fluticasone furoate-umeclidinium-vilanterol (triple)
drugs.notes: Exacerbations on LABA+LAMA with eosinophils 100 cells/microL or more.

drugs.name: Azithromycin
drugs.dose: 250 mg orally once daily, or 500 mg three times a week, for 1 year
drugs.notes: Non-smokers with continued exacerbations; check QTc and hearing; consider resistance.

drugs.name: Roflumilast
drugs.notes: FEV1 below 50%, chronic bronchitis, prior hospitalised exacerbation. Diarrhoea, weight loss; caution in depression.

drugs.name: Dupilumab
drugs.notes: On triple therapy, chronic bronchitis, eosinophils 300 cells/microL or more.

drugs.name: Mepolizumab
drugs.notes: On triple therapy with eosinophilic phenotype.

sources.title: Global Strategy for the Diagnosis, Management, and Prevention of COPD, 2026 report
